plain: In the Republic, the ancient Greek philosopher Plato tells the Myth of Er, about a soldier who dies in battle and then returns to tell what he saw beyond death. The religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka calls it one of the earliest recorded near-death experiences, "the soldier who dies in battle and has a near-death experience." The philosopher James Madden tells it too, as a reader of Plato. He describes Er as "a virtuous person" who "dies in battle for the city," and does not frame it as a near-death experience. Both bring it up on Jesse Michels's show to suggest that accounts of consciousness surviving death are very old. The two differ only in how they frame Er: as an early case of a modern experience, or as a moral tale about a good man.
